question.problem: Consider the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-x-2y-2z \\ -z \\ x+2y+3z\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $\,u=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ k \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $\,k\,$ such that $\,u\in \text{Ker}(T).$
question.worked_solution:
A vector $u$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $T$ if $T(u)=0.$ 

So, we need to solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(u) & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}-(-6)-2\cdot k-2\cdot 0 \\ -0 \\ -6+2\cdot k+3\cdot 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6-2k \\ 0 \\ -6+2k\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}6-2k=0 \\ -6+2k=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to these two equations is $k=3.$
